pages.text: Before books and notebooks, people told stories with pictures on cave walls.
These drawings showed animals, hunts, and daily life. Pictures helped share ideas.
Over time, pictures became symbols. Symbols could stand for objects or actions.
In ancient Mesopotamia, people pressed symbols into soft clay tablets.
After drying in the sun, the clay hardened, keeping the message safe.
In ancient China, people invented paper, making writing lighter and easier to carry.
Instead of drawing whole pictures, alphabets used letters to represent sounds.
With letters, people could write many different words and ideas.
Writing allowed people to record laws, trade, stories, and history.
From cave pictures to books, writing changed how humans shared knowledge forever.
